cards.back: Two numbers that add up to a total. 3 and 7 are a number bond for 10.
cards.say: A number bond. Two numbers that add up to a total. Three and seven are a number bond for ten.
One plus what equals ten? Nine. One and nine make ten.
Two plus what equals ten? Eight. Two and eight make ten.
Three plus what equals ten? Seven. Three and seven make ten.
Four plus what equals ten? Six. Four and six make ten.
Five plus what equals ten? Five. Five and five make ten.
Six plus what equals ten? Four. Six and four make ten.
Seven plus what equals ten? Three. Seven and three make ten.
Eight plus what equals ten? Two. Eight and two make ten.
Nine plus what equals ten? One. Nine and one make ten.
Zero plus what equals ten? Ten. Zero and ten make ten.

cards.front: A ten frame has 10 boxes. 6 are full. How many are empty?
cards.say: A ten frame has ten boxes. Six are full. How many are empty? Four. Six and four make ten.

cards.front: Which pair makes 10? 2 and 8, 3 and 6, or 4 and 4?
cards.say: Which pair makes ten? Two and eight. Three and six make nine. Four and four make eight.

cards.back: 7. 3 and 7 make 10, so 10 take away 3 is 7.
cards.say: Ten take away three equals seven. Three and seven make ten.

cards.back: 4. 6 and 4 make 10, so 10 take away 6 is 4.
cards.say: Ten take away six equals four. Six and four make ten.

cards.back: 2. 8 and 2 make 10, so 10 take away 8 is 2.
cards.say: Ten take away eight equals two. Eight and two make ten.
Eight plus five. Split five into two and three. Eight plus two equals ten, then ten plus three equals thirteen.
Nine plus four. Split four into one and three. Nine plus one equals ten, then ten plus three equals thirteen.
Seven plus six. Split six into three and three. Seven plus three equals ten, then ten plus three equals thirteen.
Six plus five. Split five into four and one. Six plus four equals ten, then ten plus one equals eleven.
Nine plus seven. Split seven into one and six. Nine plus one equals ten, then ten plus six equals sixteen.
